hints: For a mask k, count input elements containing every bit of k.
Every nonempty subset of those elements has AND containing k.
Invert these superset counts to recover the number with AND exactly k.
analogy: First count all subsets whose AND includes a required set of bits, then subtract those with extra bits.
example: For [1,3], nonempty subset ANDs are 1,3,1, so exact counts at 0 through 3 are 0,2,0,1.
algorithm: Choose B bits covering all values and compute superset frequencies with a sum-over-subsets transform. For each mask set F[mask]=2^(count[mask])-1 modulo 10^9+7. Apply the inverse superset transform by subtracting the corresponding higher-bit entries. Output exact counts for masks 0 through n.
correctness: F[mask] counts exactly nonempty subsets whose AND is a supermask of mask. Superset inversion subtracts every strict-supermask contribution and leaves each exact AND count.
complexity: For n elements and B bits, O(n+B*2^B) time and O(2^B) space.
